Dated this 18th day of March, 2022

1. NAME OF THE SOCIETY

The name of the Society shall be "Nilgiri Eastern Slopes Wildlife Trust", hereinafter referred to as "the Trust".

2. REGISTERED OFFICE

The registered office of the Trust shall be situated at No. 14, Kateri Road, Coonoor, The Nilgiris District, Tamil Nadu 643101. The registered office may be shifted within the limits of Coonoor town by a resolution of the Governing Body, with due intimation to the Registrar of Societies.

3. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES

The aims and objectives for which the Trust is established are as follows:

a) To work for the conservation of wildlife and the protection of natural habitats in the Nilgiri Eastern Slopes landscape, including the reserve forests, shola-grassland ecosystems, and riparian corridors that fall within the districts of The Nilgiris, Erode, and Coimbatore in the State of Tamil Nadu.

b) To undertake scientific research and monitoring of wildlife populations, with particular emphasis on large mammals, birds, amphibians, and butterflies endemic to the Western Ghats.

c) To document and map the distribution of flora and fauna in the region, and to maintain a repository of such data for use by researchers, forest departments, and policy makers.

d) To assist the State Forest Department and other statutory bodies in the implementation of wildlife management plans, including the mitigation of human-wildlife conflict.

e) To undertake habitat restoration activities, including the removal of invasive alien plant species, the planting of native tree species, and the restoration of degraded shola forest and grassland patches.

f) To organise awareness programmes, nature camps, and training workshops for local communities, school children, and college students, to foster a culture of conservation among the people of the Nilgiris.

g) To provide technical support and capacity building to frontline forest staff, including the supply of field equipment and the conduct of training sessions on wildlife monitoring and rescue.

h) To cooperate and collaborate with other non-governmental organisations, research institutions, and government agencies, both within India and abroad, having similar aims and objectives.

i) To undertake the rescue, treatment, and rehabilitation of injured, orphaned, or displaced wildlife, in accordance with the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and the rules framed thereunder, and to operate a wildlife rehabilitation centre for this purpose.

j) To raise funds by way of grants, donations, membership fees, and other lawful means, and to apply such funds towards the furtherance of the above objectives.

k) To purchase, take on lease, or otherwise acquire movable and immovable property as may be necessary for the furtherance of the objectives of the Trust.
Your designation shall be Chief Wildlife Veterinarian. This is a full-time, permanent position within the Trust's establishment, reporting directly to the Executive Director. Your designation is current and effective from the date of joining, and shall remain in force until such time as it is revised by mutual consent or superseded by a subsequent order of the Board of Trustees.

2. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

The Trust acknowledges the following qualifications and professional experience, which formed the basis of your selection:

a) Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry (B.V.Sc. & A.H.) from Madras Veterinary College, Tamil Nadu Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, Chennai, completed in May 2012.

b) Master of Veterinary Science (M.V.Sc.) in Veterinary Surgery and Radiology from the Indian Veterinary Research Institute, Izatnagar, Uttar Pradesh, completed in July 2015.

c) Postgraduate Diploma in Wildlife Medicine and Rehabilitation from the Wildlife Institute of India, Dehradun, completed in December 2016.

d) Seven years of prior professional experience, including four years as a Veterinary Officer with the Tamil Nadu Forest Department (Mobile Veterinary Unit, Coimbatore Division) and three years as a Consulting Veterinarian with the Wildlife Trust of India's Rapid Action Project in the Nilgiris Eastern Ghats landscape.

e) Valid registration with the Tamil Nadu Veterinary Council (Registration No. TNVC/VO/2012/3847), renewed up to March 2026.

3. REPORTING STRUCTURE

You shall report to the Executive Director of the Trust. In the absence of the Executive Director, you shall report to the Deputy Director (Operations). You shall function in close coordination with the following personnel:

a) The Field Coordinator (Rescue and Rehabilitation), for matters relating to wildlife rescue operations and the day-to-day functioning of the rehabilitation centre.

Dr. Ananya Raghavan's designation is Chief Wildlife Veterinarian. Record status: current.

b) The Research Officer, for matters relating to disease surveillance, epidemiological studies, and the collection of biological samples.

c) The Administrative Officer, for matters relating to procurement of veterinary supplies, maintenance of equipment, and record-keeping.

You shall also maintain professional liaison with the Chief Wildlife Warden's Office, Tamil Nadu Forest Department, and with the veterinary officers of the Forest Department's Mobile Veterinary Units operating in the Nilgiris, Erode, and Coimbatore districts.

4. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Your primary responsibilities as Chief Wildlife Veterinarian shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

a) To plan, organise, and supervise all veterinary activities of the Trust, including the rescue, treatment, rehabilitation, and release of injured, orphaned, or displaced wildlife, in accordance with the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the rules framed thereunder.

b) To provide clinical veterinary care, including but not limited to emergency first aid, surgical intervention, anaesthesia, radiology, and post-operative management, for wildlife admitted to the Trust's rehabilitation centre at Mettupalayam and at any satellite facility that may be established.

c) To develop and implement standard operating procedures for wildlife capture, handling, transportation, and restraint, with due regard to animal welfare and the safety of field staff.

d) To conduct regular health assessments of animals under the Trust's care, maintain detailed medical records for each individual animal, and ensure that such records are updated within 48 hours of any clinical event.

e) To advise the Executive Director and the Board of Trustees on matters of wildlife health policy, zoonotic disease risks, and the feasibility of release of rehabilitated animals into the wild.
a) To plan, coordinate, and lead wildlife rescue operations in the eastern slopes of the Nilgiris, including the areas around Coonoor, Kotagiri, Mettupalayam, and the forest fringes of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve.

b) To receive and respond to rescue intimation calls from the public, Forest Department officials, and other agencies, and to ensure that the Trust's rescue vehicle and team are dispatched with minimum delay.

c) To assess the situation on site, determine the species and condition of the animal, and take appropriate action for safe capture, restraint, and transport to the Trust's rehabilitation centre at Mettupalayam.

e) To maintain a field diary and rescue log for every operation, recording the date, time, location (with GPS coordinates), species, animal condition, action taken, and names of personnel involved. The rescue log shall be submitted to the Executive Director within 48 hours of the conclusion of each operation.

f) To assist the Chief Wildlife Veterinarian in the handling, restraint, and transportation of animals undergoing treatment or rehabilitation.

g) To lead release operations for rehabilitated animals, including site selection, transport, post-release monitoring, and documentation, in accordance with the guidelines of the Chief Wildlife Warden's Office.

h) To coordinate with the Tamil Nadu Forest Department, the Police Department, and local panchayats as necessary for the safe conduct of rescue and release operations.

i) To train and supervise the Field Assistants attached to the rescue team, and to ensure that they adhere to the Trust's standard operating procedures for wildlife handling and safety.

j) To undertake any other duties as may be assigned by the Executive Director from time to time, consistent with the objectives of the Trust.

**4. REMUNERATION AND ALLOWANCES**

a) Your consolidated monthly salary shall be ₹28,000 (Rupees Twenty-Eight Thousand only) per month, payable on the last working day of each month.

b) You shall be entitled to a field allowance of ₹200 per day for days on which you are deployed on rescue or release operations outside the Mettupalayam headquarters, subject to a maximum of 10 days per month.

c) The Trust shall reimburse actual and reasonable expenses incurred on mobile phone usage, as per the reimbursement policy in force.

d) The Trust shall provide the use of the rescue vehicle for official purposes only. Private use of the vehicle is not permitted.

**5. LEAVE**

a) You shall be entitled to 12 days of casual leave and 12 days of earned leave per calendar year, to be availed in accordance with the Trust's leave rules.

b) Since rescue operations are often required outside normal working hours and on holidays, you shall be entitled to compensatory off for any work performed on Sundays or declared public holidays, to be credited to your leave account.

**6. TERMINATION**

a) During the probationary period, the services of the employee may be terminated by either party by giving one month's notice in writing, or by payment of one month's salary in lieu of notice.

b) After confirmation, the services of the employee may be terminated by either party by giving three months' notice in writing, or by payment of three months' salary in lieu of notice.

c) The Trust reserves the right to terminate your services with immediate effect if you are found to have committed any act of gross misconduct, fraud, or violation of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

**7. CODE OF CONDUCT**

a) You shall conduct yourself in a manner befitting a representative of the Trust and shall not bring the Trust into disrepute.

Mr. Karthik presented a summary of the field activities undertaken between November 2022 and January 2023. The patrols were primarily focused on monitoring elephant movement corridors and checking for signs of poaching or illegal logging. No major offences were recorded, though two instances of cattle encroachment were noted near the forest fringe and were reported to the Forest Department.

Dr. Nair requested details on any animal health issues observed during the patrols. Mr. Karthik noted that a sub-adult male elephant with a limp was sighted near the Kallar river on 2023-01-15. Dated this 18th day of March, 2022

1. NAME OF THE SOCIETY

The name of the Society shall be "Nilgiri Eastern Slopes Wildlife Trust", hereinafter referred to as "the Trust".

2. REGISTERED OFFICE

The registered office of the Trust shall be situated at No. 14, Kateri Road, Coonoor, The Nilgiris District, Tamil Nadu 643101. The registered office may be shifted within the limits of Coonoor town by a resolution of the Governing Body, with due intimation to the Registrar of Societies.

3. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES

The aims and objectives for which the Trust is established are as follows:

a) To work for the conservation of wildlife and the protection of natural habitats in the Nilgiri Eastern Slopes landscape, including the reserve forests, shola-grassland ecosystems, and riparian corridors that fall within the districts of The Nilgiris, Erode, and Coimbatore in the State of Tamil Nadu.

b) To undertake scientific research and monitoring of wildlife populations, with particular emphasis on large mammals, birds, amphibians, and butterflies endemic to the Western Ghats.

c) To document and map the distribution of flora and fauna in the region, and to maintain a repository of such data for use by researchers, forest departments, and policy makers.

d) To assist the State Forest Department and other statutory bodies in the implementation of wildlife management plans, including the mitigation of human-wildlife conflict.

e) To undertake habitat restoration activities, including the removal of invasive alien plant species, the planting of native tree species, and the restoration of degraded shola forest and grassland patches.

f) To organise awareness programmes, nature camps, and training workshops for local communities, school children, and college students, to foster a culture of conservation among the people of the Nilgiris.

g) To provide technical support and capacity building to frontline forest staff, including the supply of field equipment and the conduct of training sessions on wildlife monitoring and rescue.

h) To cooperate and collaborate with other non-governmental organisations, research institutions, and government agencies, both within India and abroad, having similar aims and objectives.

i) To undertake the rescue, treatment, and rehabilitation of injured, orphaned, or displaced wildlife, in accordance with the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and the rules framed thereunder, and to operate a wildlife rehabilitation centre for this purpose.

j) To raise funds by way of grants, donations, membership fees, and other lawful means, and to apply such funds towards the furtherance of the above objectives.

k) To purchase, take on lease, or otherwise acquire movable and immovable property as may be necessary for the furtherance of the objectives of the Trust.

e) Valid registration with the Tamil Nadu Veterinary Council (Registration No. TNVC/VO/2012/3847), renewed up to March 2026.

3. REPORTING STRUCTURE

You shall report to the Executive Director of the Trust. In the absence of the Executive Director, you shall report to the Deputy Director (Operations). You shall function in close coordination with the following personnel:

a) The Field Coordinator (Rescue and Rehabilitation), for matters relating to wildlife rescue operations and the day-to-day functioning of the rehabilitation centre.

b) The Research Officer, for matters relating to disease surveillance, epidemiological studies, and the collection of biological samples.

c) The Administrative Officer, for matters relating to procurement of veterinary supplies, maintenance of equipment, and record-keeping.

You shall also maintain professional liaison with the Chief Wildlife Warden's Office, Tamil Nadu Forest Department, and with the veterinary officers of the Forest Department's Mobile Veterinary Units operating in the Nilgiris, Erode, and Coimbatore districts.

4. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Your primary responsibilities as Chief Wildlife Veterinarian shall include, but not be limited to, the following:

a) To plan, organise, and supervise all veterinary activities of the Trust, including the rescue, treatment, rehabilitation, and release of injured, orphaned, or displaced wildlife, in accordance with the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the rules framed thereunder.

b) To provide clinical veterinary care, including but not limited to emergency first aid, surgical intervention, anaesthesia, radiology, and post-operative management, for wildlife admitted to the Trust's rehabilitation centre at Mettupalayam and at any satellite facility that may be established.

**9. PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL REPORTS – 2022**

The following performance appraisal reports pertain to the calendar year 2022. Appraisals were conducted in accordance with the Trust’s Staff Evaluation Policy, revised on 2022-01-05. Each report was reviewed by the Director, Dr. S. Ramanathan, and countersigned by the respective staff member. Ratings are on a five-point scale: 5 – Outstanding, 4 – Very Good, 3 – Good, 2 – Needs Improvement, 1 – Unsatisfactory. Overall ratings reflect performance during the period 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31.

**MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE FIELD AND VETERINARY STAFF**

**Nilgiri Eastern Slopes Wildlife Trust (NESWT)**

**Date:** 2023-02-06
**Time:** 10:00 hours to 12:30 hours
**Venue:** Trust Office, Coonoor
**Chairperson:** Mr. S. Ramanathan, Director
**Secretary:** Ms. M. Ananya, Veterinary Assistant (minutes recorded)

**Attendees:**

1.  Mr. S. Ramanathan – Director
2.  Dr. Priya Nair – Veterinary Officer
3.  Mr. R. Karthik – Field Officer
4.  Ms. M. Ananya – Veterinary Assistant
5.  Mr. S. Prakash – Field Assistant
6.  Mr. V. Subramani – Driver cum Field Assistant
7.  Ms. K. Lakshmi – Office Manager

**Apologies:** None recorded.

**Agenda:**

1.  Review of the 2022-2023 winter season field operations.
2.  Status of the elephant calf rehabilitation programme.
3.  Equipment and vehicle maintenance report.
4.  Staff training and capacity building for the upcoming year.
5.  Budget utilisation and procurement plan for the first quarter of 2023.
6.  Any other business.

---

**1. Review of the 2022-2023 Winter Season Field Operations**

Mr. Karthik presented a summary of the field activities undertaken between November 2022 and January 2023. He reported that a total of 14 patrols were conducted in the eastern slopes region, covering the Mettupalayam and Coonoor ranges. The patrols were primarily focused on monitoring elephant movement corridors and checking for signs of poaching or illegal logging. No major offences were recorded, though two instances of cattle encroachment were noted near the forest fringe and were reported to the Forest Department.

Dr. Nair requested details on any animal health issues observed during the patrols. Mr. Karthik noted that a sub-adult male elephant with a limp was sighted near the Kallar river on 2023-01-15. The animal was observed for a period of 20 minutes and appeared to be feeding normally. The sighting was logged in the field diary, and a follow-up patrol was conducted on 2023-01-22, but the animal was not re-sighted. Dr. Nair advised that the field staff should continue to report any such observations and that a photographic record would be helpful for future reference.

**Decision:** The patrol schedule for February and March 2023 was approved as presented. Mr. Karthik will ensure that field diaries are submitted to the office on a weekly basis.

**Action Item 1:** Mr. R. Karthik to submit the consolidated patrol report for January 2023 to the Director’s office by 2023-02-10.

---

**2. Status of the Elephant Calf Rehabilitation Programme**

Dr. Nair provided a detailed update on the rehabilitation of the orphaned male elephant calf currently under the Trust’s care. The calf, estimated to be 14 months old, was rescued from a private estate near Mettupalayam on 2022-10-18 and has been housed at the temporary rehabilitation enclosure since then.

The calf’s weight was recorded as 385 kg on 2023-02-01, showing a steady gain of approximately 2.5 kg per week over the last month. Its diet consists of milk formula, supplemented with tender bamboo shoots, elephant grass, and boiled ragi. The calf is reported to be active and responsive to its handlers. Dr. Nair stated that the calf’s health is currently stable, and a full veterinary examination is scheduled for 2023-02-15 to assess its growth and development.

Ms. Ananya noted that the calf’s feeding schedule has been standardised to four feeds per day, at 06:00, 10:00, 14:00, and 18:00 hours. She also reported that the enclosure fencing was inspected on 2023-01-28 and was found to be secure, with no signs of damage.

**Decision:** The rehabilitation protocol will continue as per the current plan. A review of the calf’s readiness for soft-release will be undertaken after the completion of the 2023-02-15 examination.

**NILGIRI EASTERN SLOPES WILDLIFE TRUST (NESWT)**
**Rescue Intake Form**
*Field Rescue Team – Coonoor Range*

---

**NESWT-2022-014**
**Date of Incident:** 2022-03-12
**Species:** ELE (Asian Elephant, *Elephas maximus*)
**Age Class:** Adult female
**Sex:** Female
**Condition:** Lacerated wound on left forelimb, approximately 12 cm long; moderate bleeding; animal ambulatory but favouring the limb. Wound appears 2–3 days old, with early maggot infestation noted at edges. Vital signs at initial visual assessment (distance ~30 m): respiration 14/min, alert. Body condition score 3/5.
**Location:** Tea estate boundary near Hillgrove, Coonoor Range (11.3532° N, 76.7951° E). Animal was moving along the edge of a *shola* fragment adjoining the estate.
**Reporter Contact:** Mr. R. Selvam, estate supervisor, mobile +91 98430 11223; reported via NESWT hotline at 06:40 IST.
**Intake Time:** 2022-03-12T08:15+05:30
**Intake Officer:** K. Rajan (Field Assistant)
**Remarks:** Photographs taken from vehicle; forest department range officer informed. Veterinary team dispatched. Animal not darted; monitoring plan initiated from a safe distance. No crop damage reported in the vicinity. Reporter stated the elephant was first seen by estate workers at dawn near the drainage line.

---

**NESWT-2022-051**
**Date of Incident:** 2022-06-28
**Species:** LPD (Leopard, *Panthera pardus*)
**Age Class:** Subadult male
**Sex:** Male
**Condition:** Trapped in a foothold snare on the right hind leg; deep circumferential laceration exposing tendon; leg swollen and non-weight-bearing. Animal dehydrated, estimated body weight 35 kg. Respiration 28/min, heart rate 112 bpm, temperature 38.9°C (taken after chemical immobilisation). Mild corneal opacity noted in left eye.
**Location:** Foothills near Mettupalayam, on the eastern slopes of the Nilgiris (11.3012° N, 76.9403° E), approximately 200 m from the nearest village habitation.
**Reporter Contact:** Mr. P. Murugan, farmer, mobile +91 98942 77810; reported at 09:15 IST on 2022-06-28.
**Intake Time:** 2022-06-28T14:40+05:30
**Intake Officer:** Dr. Meera Krishnan (Veterinary Officer)
**Remarks:** Snare removed at site after immobilisation with medetomidine-ketamine; wound flushed and dressed. Animal transported in a transport cage to the NESWT rehabilitation facility at Mettupalayam. Forest department permission obtained (letter ref. FD/2022/118). Prognosis guarded due to tendon involvement. Follow-up radiographs scheduled.

Rescue Intake Form required_fields date of incident, species, age class, sex, condition, location, reporter contact, intake time. Record status: current.

---

**NESWT-2022-077**
**Date of Incident:** 2022-08-19
**Species:** HBL (Malabar Grey Hornbill, *Ocyceros griseus*)
**Age Class:** Adult
**Sex:** Female
**Condition:** Fractured right wing (mid-humerus, closed); mild feather loss over the dorsum; alert and responsive. Body weight 0.48 kg. No external wounds or bleeding. Crop full of *ficus* fruits at intake.
**Location:** Roadside near Burliyar, Coonoor–Mettupalayam Road (11.3219° N, 76.8217° E). Bird was found by a passerby after apparently colliding with a vehicle or a branch.
**Reporter Contact:** Ms. A. Fernandes, teacher, mobile +91 98801 44567; reported at 17:20 IST on 2022-08-19.
**Intake Time:** 2022-08-19T18:05+05:30
**Intake Officer:** Dr. Ananya Iyer (Veterinary Officer)
**Remarks:** Radiographs taken at intake; humeral fracture confirmed, no comminution. Wing bandaged in figure-of-eight splint. Bird housed in a quiet, low-stress enclosure. Hand-fed figs and mealworms; droppings normal. Prognosis fair for release after 4–6 weeks, pending feather regrowth and flight assessment.

**NESWT-2022-089**
**Date of Incident:** 2022-09-14
**Species:** LPD (Leopard, *Panthera pardus*)
**Age Class:** Sub-adult (estimated 18–24 months)

**Condition:** Trapped in a foothold snare on the left forelimb; deep laceration with exposed flexor tendons, moderate swelling and necrosis of the wound margins. Dehydrated (skin tent 3–4 sec), body weight 24.5 kg. Rectal temperature 38.9°C, heart rate 96 bpm, respiratory rate 28/min. No fractures detected on palpation or radiograph.
**Location:** Coffee estate near Ithalar, Coonoor taluk (11.3524° N, 76.8712° E), approximately 1.5 km from the nearest settlement.
**Reporter Contact:** Mr. R. Thangavel, estate supervisor, mobile +91 97876 33210; reported at 08:40 IST on 2022-09-14.
**Intake Time:** 2022-09-14T13:15+05:30
**Intake Officer:** Dr. Meera Krishnan (Veterinary Officer)
**Remarks:** Animal immobilised with medetomidine-ketamine at the site. Snare wire removed; wound debrided under anaesthesia and flushed with dilute povidone-iodine. Tendons assessed as intact but contused. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (amoxicillin-clavulanate) and meloxicam administered. Transported in a crush cage to the NESWT facility. Forest department permission letter ref. FD/2022/214 attached. Prognosis fair to guarded; daily wound lavage planned for the first week.

---

**NESWT-2022-094**
**Date of Incident:** 2022-10-02
**Species:** ELE (Asian Elephant, *Elephas maximus*)
**Age Class:** Adult (female, estimated 25–30 years)
**Sex:** Female
**Condition:** Gunshot wound on the right shoulder region, entry wound approx. 2 cm diameter with a suspected bullet track directed cranio-ventrally; exit wound not identified. Moderate swelling and serosanguinous discharge. Animal recumbent at the time of initial report but able to stand with assistance. Body condition poor (ribs and spine visible). Body weight not obtained due to animal size and condition; estimated 2,800 kg.
**Location:** Forest edge near Kottamalai, Mettupalayam range (11.2851° N, 76.8827° E), adjacent to a banana plantation.
**Reporter Contact:** Mr. S. Karuppusamy, plantation owner, mobile +91 98430 55678; reported at 06:50 IST on 2022-10-02.
**Intake Time:** 2022-10-02T11:30+05:30
**Intake Officer:** Dr. Ananya Iyer (Veterinary Officer)
**Remarks:** Animal darted with etorphine at 10:15 IST. Wound explored and flushed; bullet fragments visible on radiographs. Debridement performed, drains placed. Wound left open for drainage; dressing changed under standing sedation. Antibiotics (ceftiofur) and flunixin meglumine administered. Animal walked into the transport truck at 12:40 IST. Forest department and Wildlife Warden permission obtained (ref. FD/2022/231). Condition critical; intensive monitoring and wound management planned. Blood samples collected for haemogram and biochemistry.

**Sex:** Unknown

**Location:** Private garden in Ketti, near the Coonoor–Ketti Road (11.3987° N, 76.6952° E).
**Reporter Contact:** Mrs. L. D'Souza, homemaker, mobile +91 94430 11223; reported at 15:10 IST on 2022-10-28.
**Intake Time:** 2022-10-28T16:20+05:30
**Intake Officer:** Dr. Ananya Iyer (Veterinary Officer)
**Remarks:** Radiographs taken; no fracture or dislocation identified. Wing strapped to the body to restrict movement. Bird housed in a sheltered enclosure with perches of varying heights. Hand-fed figs, papaya, and mealworms; droppings normal. Prognosis good for release after 2–3 weeks, pending flight assessment.
